text.p: - Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

-Thirteen out of 16 local labour party leaders want a more liberal policy towards refugees and people applying for political asylum. The demand for reforms is expected to be a main issue at the labour party's annual conference, which begins on Thursday.

-The large commercial banks are unlikely to follow the central bank's cut in interest rates. Norges Bank announced a 0.5 percent reduction in key interest rates on Tuesday to try and dampen the rapid appreciation in the Norwegian crown.
-Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg says the rate cut demands even more discipline in this year's budget negotiations in parliament. He stresses the importance of a tight fiscal policy.
-Insurer Gjensidige has gained market share in both the insurance and banking market. However profits in the first nine months 1996 were lower than in the same year-ago period.

-Decommissioning nuclear power plants in Sweden will lead to higher electricity prices in Norway, concludes a research study by the Swedish Power Plants Association. The study says levels od carbon dioxide emissions will increase considerably as a consequence of convertion to fossil fuel.
